item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) is deploying artificial intelligence to check electronically entered election result figures against scanned result sheets before upload, as Nigeria prepares for the 2027 general election. The move is part of efforts to reduce human error and strengthen electoral transparency, amid growing concerns that AI-generated misinformation, cloned videos and synthetic voices could undermine voters’ confidence in the electoral process. The chatbot provides government information in English, Hausa, Igbo and Yoruba, a model she said could be adapted to help voters access reliable information about registration, polling units and election procedures. “Build something that makes the truth easier to find than falsehood,” she challenged developers. The programme’s convener, Dr Toyosi Akerele-Ogunsiji, said the initiative would bring together developers, researchers, journalists, election experts and civil society organisations to build functional solutions to electoral challenges ahead of 2027. She said the programme followed the development of Run-Am, an AI-powered misinformation detection and fact-checking application created for Nigeria’s 2023 elections. The new initiative will focus on trustworthy electoral information, data analysis, inclusive and multilingual civic technology, cybersecurity, election observation and citizen accountability. It will also include an AI Innovations Development Hub and a Community of Practice to support promising solutions beyond the hackathon. Applications opened on Thursday, October 22, and will close on November 12, 2026. Eligible Nigerians aged 18 and above may apply individually or in teams of up to four. The competition has a N10 million prize pool, with N4 million for the overall winner, N2.5 million for second place and N1.5 million for third place, alongside four special awards worth N500,000 each. Professor Victor Odumuyiwa of the University of Lagos urged INEC to prioritise homegrown solutions, arguing that Nigerian developers were better placed to understand the country’s electoral challenges. “We understand our context, we know the problems, and we are the ones best placed to solve them,” he said. Lawyer Tsema Ede, who addressed the legal and ethical implications of AI in elections, said the technology offered opportunities for voter education, electoral malpractice monitoring and cybersecurity but required safeguards against misuse. The organisers said the programme would remain non-partisan, barring projects designed to influence voter preferences or interfere with electoral administration. Unauthorised testing of live electoral systems is also prohibited, while winning the competition will not automatically authorise operational deployment. The initiative will culminate in a national grand finale in Lagos on December 16, followed by technical support for selected innovations. item.title: 2027: Makinde knocks Tinubu over budget implementation
item.description: — Says Nigeria needs reset, urges government to tax prosperity, not poverty By Dayo Johnson AKURE — The African Peoples Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has criticised President Bola Tinubu’s administration over what he described as poor implementation of the national budget, promising to reset Nigeria’s security architecture, economy and political system if elected in 2027. Makinde, who spoke at the APM South-West town hall meeting in Akure, Ondo State, said Nigeria was not functioning as it should, blaming weak budget implementation and an unproductive economy for the country’s persistent challenges. He also advocated a tax system that places greater emphasis on prosperity rather than poverty, arguing that government should prioritise policies that enable Nigerians to become productive and financially secure. “I said, please, let the people be productive. When they are productive, they become prosperous. When they become prosperous, tax their prosperity. Do not tax poverty,” he said. He warned that such an approach could leave projects unfinished from one administration to another, preventing the country from deriving full value from its resources. 1999 precedent Addressing concerns about contesting the presidency when the incumbent president is from the South-West, Makinde cited the 1999 presidential election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae contested against each other despite both being from the region. He said the contest demonstrated that the South-West could present multiple candidates and allow Nigerians to choose their preferred leader. “In 1999, when the entire country ceded the presidency to the South-West, we had two of our fathers, Baba President Olusegun Obasanjo and Baba Olu Falae, contesting for the presidency. Both were from the South-West, and heaven did not fall,” he said. Makinde added that Nigeria’s challenges required collective action across regions, rather than an approach based on political entitlement or the belief that a particular region should automatically retain power. He also criticised what he described as the use of political power to weaken opposition parties, insisting that a functioning democracy required an open political space. “I do not understand how a party in power, with 31 governors and almost all the instruments of coercion at its disposal, can still be afraid of the opposition. It will not allow the opposition to thrive,” he said. He called on the Federal Government to stop actions that he alleged were creating crises for opposition parties, adding that “there is no democracy in a one-party system.” Security, economic reforms On security, Makinde said Nigeria needed to overhaul its security architecture to create an environment in which businesses could operate beyond the current constraints imposed by insecurity. He said his administration, if elected, would work to expand economic activity and reduce the country’s dependence on federal allocations as the principal source of revenue for states and local governments. Makinde also reiterated his call for the Federal Government to remit funds due to states and local governments from the Nigeria Liquefied Natural Gas (NLNG) revenue, saying the reconciliation of the figures had been completed. He said the Reset Nigeria agenda would seek to make the economy more productive and create multiple pathways for lifting citizens out of poverty. The APM candidate urged South-West residents to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards and support his presidential ambition, describing himself as a “reset agent”. He also proposed that an APM-led administration would constitute a transitional government of national unity to reposition the country for prosperity. APM offers alternative Earlier, the party’s National Chairman, Mamman Dantalle, said the APM was offering Nigerians an alternative to the country’s current political and economic direction ahead of the 2027 general election. Dantalle urged voters to assess candidates based on their experience, competence and capacity to deliver, rather than their financial resources or age. He identified insecurity as a major national concern, saying many Nigerians were afraid of travelling, visiting markets or going to their farms because of the risk of kidnapping. The party chairman argued that insecurity was linked to broader socio-economic problems, including poverty, inequality, poor living conditions and hopelessness. “These kidnappers are not unknown individuals. They live among us. They are our brothers. They are our family members. They are our friends,” he said. He added that some conventional crimes reflected deeper problems in the country’s socio-economic and political arrangements. “Sociologically, some of these conventional crimes are not the problem. They are only indications that something is wrong with the socio-economic and political arrangement. And what is that? Inequality, poverty, squalor and hopelessness,” he said. Also speaking, Bauchi State Governor Bala Mohammed said Nigeria needed leaders with the vision, knowledge and capacity to unlock the potential of its different regions. Mohammed highlighted the economic importance of the South-South, particularly its natural resources, but said the region required leadership capable of translating its wealth into improved living standards. He said the APM candidates offered an opportunity to pursue a different direction through planning, consultation and public participation. item.title: 2027: Jandor targets 3m votes for Tinubu, Hamzat
item.description: — Sanwo-Olu, Obasa, Ojelabi, Edun urge grassroots mobilisation By Olasunkanmi Akoni LAGOS — Convener of the Lagos4Lagos Movement, Olajide Adediran, popularly known as Jandor, has inaugurated a support group for President Bola Tinubu, Lagos State governorship candidate Dr Obafemi Hamzat and other All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates, targeting more than three million votes for the party in the state in the 2027 elections. The JANDOR Support Group for PBAT-KOH 2027 was inaugurated on Thursday at the Eko FM Marquee, Lagos Television premises, Agidingbi, Ikeja, with party leaders, local government chairmen, traditional rulers and members of the Lagos4Lagos Movement in attendance. Adediran, the group’s lead visioner, said the initiative was established to fulfil his commitment to support whoever emerged as the APC’s candidate and contribute to the party’s electoral mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. Speaking to journalists after the inauguration, Jandor said the move followed his withdrawal from the Lagos governorship race after the party’s candidate-selection process. He said the Lagos4Lagos Movement’s structure had been aligned with the APC from the state executive level to senatorial districts, local governments and wards. According to him, two representatives from each polling unit would be inaugurated separately at the local-government level to canvass support for APC candidates in the presidential and governorship elections. Adediran stressed that the group was designed to complement, not compete with, the party’s main campaign council. He urged members to respect the party’s leadership structure and persuade voters through peaceful engagement rather than intimidation or insults. The former governorship aspirant also called on members to place the party’s collective interest above personal ambitions and extend mobilisation to markets, motor parks, workplaces, religious communities and neighbourhoods. “That declaration was not made casually. It was a statement of our belief in party supremacy, internal democracy, discipline and the greater interest of our political family,” he said, referring to his earlier commitment to support the party after the selection of its candidate. item.title: Navy to establish research institute for indigenous technology
item.description: …Abbas seeks stronger local capacity to cut costs, boost combat readiness By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Nigerian Navy has commenced plans to establish a research institute and research and development units across its commands to develop indigenous military technology, reduce operational costs and strengthen its combat capabilities. The Chief of the Naval Staff (CNS), Vice Admiral Idi Abbas, disclosed this on Thursday while delivering the keynote address at the Nigerian Navy’s 2026 Research and Development Seminar at the Naval Headquarters, Abuja. Abbas said the initiatives were aimed at institutionalising innovation, harnessing the ingenuity of naval personnel and translating research into practical, affordable solutions to operational challenges. He called for increased investment in indigenous research and development, emerging technologies and strategic partnerships to improve the Navy’s operational effectiveness and strengthen national security. item.title: ‘You have another son in me,’ Obi tells slain supporter’s mother
item.description: — NDC candidate pledges continued support to bereaved family By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has pledged continued support to the family of Ifeanyi Nwolie, his supporter who was shot dead during a political activity in Enugu State. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday while attending Nwolie’s burial in his hometown of Afa, Udi Local Government Area of Enugu State, telling the deceased’s mother that she had gained another son in him. According to reports from the event, Obi also pledged to continue the monthly financial support Nwolie had been providing for his mother and sent the family an amount covering 15 months, through December 2027. Nwolie was among supporters who participated in an NDC political activity on October 10, 2026, which was marred by violence. He was shot dead during the incident. In a post on his X handle, Obi said he arrived at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, from the United Kingdom at 5:30 a.m. on Thursday before connecting to a 7 a.m. flight to Enugu to attend the burial. He described Nwolie’s death as a painful reminder of the human cost of political violence in the country. “My humble pledge to the mother is that God Almighty, whom it pleased to bring Ifeanyi home, has also given her another son in me to support her, as Ifeanyi used to,” Obi said. As the country prepares for the 2027 general elections, the former Anambra State governor called on candidates at the federal, state and local government levels to reject violence, ethnic division and religious bigotry. He urged political parties and candidates to focus their campaigns on issues capable of improving the country, stressing that citizens must be able to express their political choices and participate in the electoral process without fear. “The process through which we attain public office is more important than the office itself,” he said. Obi also emphasised the importance of the rule of law, warning that undermining it could lead to disorder and anarchy. He called for collective efforts to build a country where human life is valued above political ambition and citizens can exercise their democratic rights in peace and safety. “A new Nigeria is possible,” he said. Wike cautioned residents against “political gamblers” and pointed to ongoing projects in the territory as the reason to stay with the Tinubu administration. On the senator representing the FCT, Ireti Kingibe, Wike asked whether anyone had felt her presence. “Today, the people of FCT, do you feel the impact? In her place, he presented Senator Philip Aduda and John Gbadaya as the coalition’s choices. “After all, party is a vehicle that conveys you to where you are going. When you get there, you come down from the vehicle and you now work for the interest of the people,” he said. Julius Adamu, the PDP chairmanship candidate in the last Area Council elections, stepped down for the Bwari Area Council Chairman, Joshua. He said a former PDP chairman once refused a ride in his car for fear that sitting in an APC member’s vehicle could cost him his position. Once its purpose was explained, 92% said hallmarking was important when buying precious-metal jewellery. For someone assessing old earrings, the hallmark can help establish the metal standard. It does not, however, determine the resale price. Are Gold-Plated Earrings Worth the Same? No. Gold-plated jewellery has a layer of gold over another material, so it should not be valued in the same way as solid gold. UK hallmarking guidance contains specific rules for describing precious-metal articles and gold-plated silver. A gold-coloured surface does not establish that an item is solid gold. Small earrings also need extra attention. Gold articles weighing less than 1 gram are exempt from compulsory hallmarking in the UK. Therefore, an unhallmarked lightweight earring is not automatically imitation jewellery. What Should You Check Before Selling Gold Earrings? Before accepting an offer to sell gold for cash, find out exactly what the buyer is paying for. The following checks can make different quotations easier to compare: Check the hallmark and fineness. Check whether testing, refining, postage or other costs are deducted. Understand whether an estimate can change after inspection. Read the payment and delivery terms before sending jewellery. Visual inspection: A buyer may examine hallmarks, maker’s marks, clasps, posts and other features alongside testing. This is also why an initial estimate can change after the jewellery has been received and assessed. Which Buyer Is Right for Your Earrings? The route depends on what gives the earrings value. Damaged or incomplete earrings may mainly be worth their gold content. A complete pair with diamonds, an established maker or antique appeal may be better suited to a jewellery-focused valuation. The purity and weight of the gold matter most, but the brand, gemstones, design and condition can also affect the price. A hallmark can help you check the gold content. The Central Bank’s figures showed year-on-year headline inflation easing to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 per cent in August. “These are positive movements. But when inflation falls, prices may still be rising, only at a slower pace. It does not mean that the cost of living has returned to what families could afford before.” Speaking further, the media chief stated, “This distinction matters for public communication. If an official says that inflation has eased, and a family hears that food is still more expensive, the family is not being unreasonable. The two statements can both be true. Good leadership explains the difference and keeps working on the effect people actually feel. “Growth must mean more than a number. It must become decent jobs, dependable public services, wages that can support a household, opportunity for young people, and confidence that the effort to build a life is worthwhile. The credibility of any economic story depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives.” Promoting Security Momoh also emphasised the need for intelligence, training, coordination, and public support to strengthen security agencies in the country. “Security is an even more immediate measure. Across the country, communities face insurgent violence, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflict, farmer–pastoralist tensions and other threats. In Adamawa and the wider North-East, insecurity has disrupted homes, farming, education, livelihoods and family life,” he said. “We must speak of these realities with care. item.description: The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention has warned that it will blacklist partners who fail to account for funds received to combat disease outbreaks on the continent. ﻿ It also warned that the era of organisations operating without transparency is over. The Director General of the Africa CDC, Dr. Jean Kaseya, stated this during an interview on Channels Television’s The Morning Brief on Thursday. He expressed displeasure that, out of the $962 million already disbursed from the $3 billion pledge made on the margins of the UN, the G20 meeting in September, some partners claimed they received around $220 million. “There was a practice in many African countries, I say many, not all, but many. Partners will get money from donors. They will implement their activities without disclosing how much they got, without even sending a report to the government,” Kaseya. “And when the outbreak is over, we’ll hear from some capitals that billions of dollars were invested to stop this outbreak. I said, enough is enough. It will never happen again on this continent. “We managed to fundraise. We got figures from all donors. Out of $3 billion pledged, based on the last meeting that the US organised in September on the margins of the UN G20 meeting, we got a total pledge of $3 billion.” “Out of that, $962 million was already disbursed. We went to work with the DRC government. We organised a meeting with partners. Only 19 out of 92 partners attended.
